capability: Account credit limits and order-time credit checking
industry_standard_baseline: B2B accounts carry a credit ceiling that is enforced, not merely displayed
current_implementation: credit_limit is capability-gated (finance.credit_limit), audited with previous and new value, and consulted server-side at order time against a defined exposure: the net ledger balance plus committed but not-yet-invoiced orders. NULL means NOT CONFIGURED, never unlimited and never zero. An over-limit order is flagged for review, not rejected
status: COMPLETE — REAL LIMITS AND CAPABILITY GRANTS OUTSTANDING
recommended_decision: Grant finance.credit_limit and finance.credit_review to the right people, then assign real limits
notes: Every account reads NULL; no numerical limits were invented. The approval workflow was completed in a later run - see PAY-015. Orders awaiting one are orders.credit_review is not null. 23 regressions injected, 22 caught; the 23rd was a semantic no-op. See 46_COMMERCIAL_CREDIT_AND_PRIVACY.md

capability: Credit review approval workflow and admin credit UI
industry_standard_baseline: Staff can maintain credit limits and resolve orders held above them, under audit
current_implementation: Finance > Credit Reviews queue with approve/decline behind finance.credit_review - a SEPARATE capability from finance.credit_limit, because approving one order must never imply raising the ceiling. Admin credit screen on Collection & Debt. Both decisions need a reason, are written in one transaction with append-only audit evidence, and the original submission snapshot is preserved rather than overwritten
recommended_decision: Grant finance.credit_review to whoever may approve an over-limit order. Nobody holds it, so the queue is unusable until then - deliberately
notes: Approving an exception NEVER changes users.credit_limit: the route issues no update to users, the response says creditLimitChanged:false, and a tamper adding the write is caught. An unapproved order cannot leave pending for fulfilment NOR be invoiced - both book the exposure the review exists to control. 25 regressions injected, 25 caught; four of the five that survived a first pass revealed real assertion gaps, which were fixed. See 47_CREDIT_OPERATIONS.md

notes: DOWNGRADED from P0 critical. The original finding was a false positive caused by a SHALLOW CLONE: .git/shallow contained 2c749ec, so git presented a grafted commit as a parentless root and merge-base could not see past it. A read-only unshallow fetch resolved every merge-base. See 33 §9 for the mechanism and the diagnostic lesson
